scope: Common synchronized interval, SI, explicit field decomposition and one signed external-work ledger

options.input: Supported C19 current I(t), plus declared clock registration and electrode terminal topology
options.constraints: Axial electrode currents I_upper=+I and I_lower=-I, with a declared conduction/displacement/plasma partition at measurement ports
options.unknowns: Conductor electrostatic gradients g_upper, g_lower and corresponding circuit voltages, solved together with evolving A/E/B and admitted conductivity/enthalpy
options.power: Sum of terminal V_port*I_port with unique signs; all field/plasma/Joule/boundary/internal transfers are internal ledger exchanges
options.potential_extension: For a short plane z_s, Phi_ext=-(z-z_s)*(g_lower+(g_upper-g_lower)*psi(x,y))+C; E_xy=(z-z_s)*(g_upper-g_lower)*grad_xy(psi), E_z=g_lower+(g_upper-g_lower)*psi. Both mixed derivatives are retained analytically, so curl E_ext=0. z_s, terminal gauge and common mode must be bound.
options.magnetic_evolution: Evolve total induced field from actual signed Jxyz, including solid conductivity and plasma; do not interpolate independent A and backward-Euler rate histories
options.thermal_feedback: Use same accepted midpoint conductivity and solid E for J_solid and sigma|E_solid|^2. Return per-cell joules once to enthalpy owner and use its returned material state on the next staged solve.
options.restriction: A z-invariant perturbation plus analytical scalar extension is a reduced model and cannot qualify axial instabilities, finite-end fringe fields, or a general 3D Maxwell solution.

options.input: Conditional remembered gap pulse V_gap(t), identified as assumed rather than measured, plus short/feed geometry and common conductor potential
options.constraints: One terminal voltage topology; infer electrode currents rather than additionally imposing C19 current
options.unknowns: Actual conductor/current response and magnetic field from the coupled plasma/solid EM solve
options.power: Voltage source work integral V_port dQ_port, including displacement and conduction at that same port exactly once; circuit inductive work must not be added again
options.potential_extension: If using the old short-to-feed linear scalar ansatz, retain Phi=2Vq(psi-1/2)+V/2 and all x,y,z derivatives together. Dropping only partial_z E_xy would create a false Faraday source.
options.magnetic_evolution: No independent old B waveform; evolve field and compare predicted current with C19 as evidence, not a second hard constraint
options.thermal_feedback: Same-interval solid current and E supply Joule heat; preserve enthalpy/material closure and rejection domain
options.restriction: The pulse is conditional and its topology/common mode require explicit binding; it does not determine all 3D conductor potentials by itself.

intermediate_pilot.approximation: Frozen DC magnetic supported-start initial state plus independent transverse gap-voltage port; ideal PEC conductors and z-invariant geometry
intermediate_pilot.use: Bounded incidence, Jxyz, boundary/circuit work and particle-field operator checks only
intermediate_pilot.not_a_claim_of: physical current-controlled or voltage-controlled resistive 60ns breakdown

required_before_physical_promotion: choose one drive constraint and terminal topology
bind full scalar/inductive background representation with paired derivatives
declare gauge and initial electric/magnetic/conductor charge state
couple dynamic conductivity/enthalpy with actual same-interval Jz and Joule energy
verify current/voltage/work, Faraday/Gauss/divB, boundary energy, time/mesh/exterior refinement
retain unknown neutral/water differential rates and material phase limits
selection_instruction: Constrain total current at a declared feed/measurement port; predict voltage; retain conduction, plasma, displacement and charge accumulation; do not enforce conditional gap pulse or solid-only current.
next_geometry: Finite axial extension with explicit feed and short topology; z-invariant intermediate cannot close transverse-breakdown current distribution.
